## Convention review of `62fc3790…HEAD` (`--review-pr` mode)

I went through all 60 rules in `rules.json`. The checklist was written to the scratchpad, not the repo, and no tracked files changed. There was no GitHub fetch, so no window and no PR or comment counts, and no docs, rules, learnings or examples were edited. I used Level 1 zoom on LOG-01, LOG-02, LOG-04, TEST-02, STYLE-01 and CONFIG-01, and no Level 2 zoom.

**Applied and passing:** SPDX headers are present on every changed file (`.env.sample.json` is JSON, so it can't carry one). DI wiring is correct, with `ZerionModule` imported and no `forwardRef` (MOD-03, MOD-05). The new limiter throws the same `LimitReachedError` as the old one, and every `catch` now rethrows it, so the error type doesn't change when the limiter is on (RESILIENCE-01). Tunables come from config and new env vars are in `.env.sample.json` (CONFIG-03, CONFIG-05). The Redis Lua counter has integration tests (CACHE-01, CACHE-02). Independent calls run in parallel (PERF-01). Totals skip non-finite values (DATA-01). Tests use the existing builders and fakes (TEST-01).

### Findings

1. **CHANGE-04 / CONFIG-01 / PR-02 — Medium: the existing rate-limit vars quietly mean something new.** `.env.sample.json:1576`, `src/modules/zerion/datasources/zerion-rate-limiter.service.ts:92`
   - `ZERION_RATE_LIMIT_CALLS_BY_PERIOD` (default `2` per 10s, `src/config/entities/configuration.ts:140`) used to limit only balances and collectibles. It now also limits positions, portfolio and the Safe overview. Any deployment on the default gets far fewer Zerion calls, and overviews will fall back to the balances repository.
   - Setting it to `0` used to block every call. The `limitCalls > 0` check now makes `0` mean "no limit".
   - The description still says only "Maximum Zerion API calls per time period". It should say the budget is shared across all Zerion datasources and that `0` disables it, the same way the new per-address var does. The default is also worth rechecking.

2. **LOG-01 / LOG-02 / LOG-03 — Medium: the fallback path logs too much, at `warn`.** `src/modules/safe/routes/v2/safes.v2.service.ts:430`, `:439`
   - `serveDegradedBalance` logs a `warn` every time the fallback succeeds, once per Safe. When Zerion is over budget, every Safe on a Zerion chain logs a `warn`, on top of the limiter's own `RateLimit` `warn` and the `debug` at `:~318`. That is an expected outcome, and LOG-02 says expected success paths shouldn't be noisy. It's a metric-style signal, so `info`/`debug` or a counter fits better.
   - When the fallback also fails, the same failure is logged twice at `warn`: once at `:439`, then again at `:138` ("Error while getting Safe overview").

3. **STYLE-01 / NAME-01 — Low: two doc comments describe the old code and will be wrong once merged.** `src/modules/safe/routes/v2/safes.v2.service.ts:182-184`
   - "(today the chain is fetched per entry)" and "dropped during the per-entry build (as today)" refer to the old behaviour.
   - Unresolved chains are now dropped in `resolveSafes` (`:161`), not in the per-entry build. The comment should name `resolveSafes`.

4. **LOG-04 — Low: the fail-open log is a plain string, not a structured log.** `src/modules/zerion/datasources/zerion-rate-limiter.service.ts:116-118`
   - The same class logs the rate-limit event as a structured `{ type: LogType.RateLimit, … }` object (`:127`), but the fail-open path interpolates `${asError(error)}` into a string. That loses the type, datasource and scope, so a Redis failure is hard to alert on.
   - It should be a structured object, e.g. `type: LogType.RateLimit, event: 'fail_open', datasource, detail: asError(error).message`, which means passing `datasource` down into `_increment`.

5. **TEST-02 — Low: the "one fetch per wallet" case is tested twice.** `src/modules/safe/routes/v2/safes.v2.service.spec.ts:107` and `src/modules/safe/routes/v2/__tests__/safes.v2.controller.overview.integration.spec.ts:312`
   - Both check that one wallet across chains 1 and 137 fetches the portfolio once and returns each chain's value. That is a service-branch rule, which the unit test already proves.
   - TEST-02 says integration tests prove wiring once per route. The integration test could shrink to a wiring smoke test, or be dropped.

6. **MOD-06 — Low, and it predates this PR: a route service calls a datasource directly.** `src/modules/safe/routes/v2/safes.v2.service.ts:268`
   - `SafesV2Service` already injected `IZerionWalletPortfolioApi`. This diff builds more on top of it: batching per wallet, handling `LimitReachedError`/`ZodError`, and importing the datasource entity type `ZerionWalletPortfolio`.
   - AGENTS.md and MOD-06 say services call repositories, never datasources. It doesn't block this PR, but a follow-up ticket to put this behind `IBalancesRepository` would stop the gap growing.

No rule outright fails.
